The criminal law has been set into motion based on the first information statement of Smt.NIMITHA.
The gist of the prosecution case is that the accused No.1 married CW-1 on 17-10- 2013.

After the marriage, when CW-1 started residing with accused No.1 at Bangalore at that time, the accused No.1 harassed CW-1 for petty matters and picked up quarrel with her and  3  C.C.No.29597/2017 harassed her physically and mentally, the other accused incited accused No.1 to do ill will acts.

On 09-07-2017 accused NO.1 picked up quarrel with respect to meal, assaulted CW-1 with his hands, when CW 1 to 3 questioned the same, the accused persons abused them in filthy language and drove CW-1 out of the house and thus subjected CW1 to mental and physical cruelty.
Based on the said information, a case in Cr.No.249/2017 came to be registered against the accused for the aforesaid offences.

 5  C.C.No.29597/2017  REASONS  9. POINT No.1 :- It is the fundamental principle of criminal jurisprudence that the prosecution has to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt.

10. CW-1 was examined as PW-1 Kumaaswamy .S.P. has deposed in his evidence that CW-1 appeared in the station and gave complaint.
He registered a case in crime No.249/2017 and submitted FIR to the court.
On the same day, at the place shown by CW1, in the presence of CW 5 and 6 he conducted spot mahazar, recorded statements of W 5 and 6 and 2 to 4.
PW-1 also deposed that after obtaining orders from the District Court, he released accused bail.
On 5-9-2017 he sent CW1 and the accused No.1 for family mediation center and thereafter completion of investigation, he submitted chargesheet against the accused.

In this case the only evidence which is available on Smt Nimitha vs Srinivas on 5 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147347760/

sentences.text: He is none other than the Investigation officer of this case.
The prosecution has failed to secure the victim and other witnesses to prove its case.
Hence, other than the formal evidence of PW1 there are no other corroborative evidence of any witnesses to prove the case of the prosecution.
The complainant herself failed to stepped into the witness box to depose about the incident, which is fatal to the prosecution case.
The available evidence of PW-1 is formal in nature and is insufficient to bring home the guilt of the accused.
Hence, this court holds that the prosecution has failed to bring home the guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt.
Accordingly, I answer Point No.1 in the Negative.

12. POINT No.2:- For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
 ORDER
In exercise of power conferred Under Section 248(1) of Cr.P.C., Accused No.1 to 4 are acquitted of the offences punishable U/s. 498A, of IPC.
C.C.No.29597/2017 The bail bonds of accused No.1 to 4 shall be in force for a period of 6 months.
